census.claim: the agent identified compound A as 3-methylcyclopentene instead of 1-isopropylidene-3-methylcyclopentane, whose ozonolysis gives 3-methylcyclopentanone and acetone
the agent claimed that H2SO4 under heat converts the alkene into the alkane methylcyclopentane instead of an acid-catalyzed addition/rearrangement product; H2SO4 does not hydrogenate a C=C bond
the agent changed the structure of A to 3-methylcyclohexene instead of the required 1-isopropylidene-3-methylcyclopentane; ozonolysis of 3-methylcyclohexene would not give cyclopentanone plus acetone
the agent claimed H2SO4/heat converts 3-methylcyclohexene into 3-methylcyclohexane instead of an acid-catalyzed addition/rearrangement product; no hydrogenation step is present

the agent identified compound A as 1-isopropenyl-3-methylcyclopentane instead of 1-isopropylidene-3-methylcyclopentane; cleavage of the isopropenyl double bond would give formaldehyde and an acetylcyclopentane, not acetone and 3-methylcyclopentanone

the agent claimed the H2SO4/heat product from A is the alkane 1-isopropyl-3-methylcyclopentane instead of an acid-catalyzed hydration/rearrangement product; protonation and rearrangement alone do not reduce the alkene to an alkane

certificates.rationale: Event_001 explicitly identifies A as 3-methylcyclopentene, but the ozonolysis products 3-methylcyclopentanone and acetone require an exocyclic isopropylidene double bond, i.e., 1-isopropylidene-3-methylcyclopentane. The claimed structure is chemically inconsistent with the given products.

Event_001 claims the H2SO4/heat product is methylcyclopentane, an alkane. Starting from an alkene, this would require hydrogenation, which sulfuric acid does not provide; the agent's protonation/rearrangement/elimination explanation cannot produce an alkane.

Event_003 changes the structure to 3-methylcyclohexene, but ozonolysis of 3-methylcyclohexene would open the six-membered ring to give an acyclic dialdehyde/ketoaldehyde product, not 3-methylcyclopentanone plus acetone.

Event_003 claims the H2SO4/heat product is 3-methylcyclohexane, an alkane. Sulfuric acid under heat does not hydrogenate an alkene to an alkane; the claimed product is not a valid acid-catalyzed addition/rearrangement outcome.

Event_004 identifies A as 1-isopropenyl-3-methylcyclopentane. Ozonolysis of an isopropenyl substituent would give formaldehyde and an acetyl-substituted cyclopentane, not acetone and 3-methylcyclopentanone. The correct structure is 1-isopropylidene-3-methylcyclopentane.

Event_004 claims the H2SO4/heat product is 1-isopropyl-3-methylcyclopentane, a saturated alkane. This would require reduction/hydrogenation of the double bond, which is not accomplished by H2SO4/heat alone, so the claimed product is chemically unsupported.

failure_analysis.failure_observation: polarity and localization both match gold
